query: What happened to the people of Ammonihah?

documents.text: But they took their armies and went over into the borders of the land of Zarahemla, and fell upon the people who were in the land of Ammonihah and destroyed them.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 25:2** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 17 verses and records Lamanite retaliation after slaying their brethren, including attacks on Ammonihah and battles with the Nephites. It reports the destruction of much of Amulon’s seed, their persecution of believing Lamanites by fire, and Lamanites then hunting Amulon’s remnant, fulfilling Abinadi’s words. Many Lamanites join Anti-Nephi-Lehi, bury weapons, keep commandments and the law of Moses while looking to Christ. Ammon and Aaron’s group rejoices.

documents.text: And thus ended the eleventh year of the judges, the Lamanites having been driven out of the land, and the people of Ammonihah were destroyed; yea, every living soul of the Ammonihahites was destroyed, and also their great city, which they said God could not destroy, because of its greatness.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 16:9** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 21 verses and records Lamanite armies destroying Ammonihah, taking captives, and Zoram with sons Lehi and Aha seeking Alma’s guidance. query: What is the Word of Wisdom?

documents.text: A WORD OF WISDOM, for the benefit of the council of high priests, assembled in Kirtland, and the church, and also the saints in Zion—
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 89:1** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 21 verses and records the Word of Wisdom given in Kirtland for the church, offered as a principle with promise. It warns against wine and strong drink (except sacramental pure wine), limits strong drink to washing, prohibits tobacco and hot drinks, and counsels use of herbs, fruits, grains, and sparing use of meat. It promises health, wisdom, strength, and protection from the destroying angel for obedient saints.

He commands readers to feast on Christ’s words, ask and knock for understanding, and states this is the doctrine of Christ until Christ manifests in the flesh. Nephi urges prayer always, warning against the evil spirit, and instructs praying to the Father in Christ’s name to consecrate actions.

documents.text: And forgive us our sins; for we also forgive every one that is indebted to us. And lead us not into temptation; but deliver us from evil.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Luke 11:4** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 54 verses and records Jesus teaching prayer (the Lord’s Prayer), urging persistence in asking, seeking, and knocking, and promising the Holy Spirit to those who ask. He casts out a mute demon, answers accusations of using Beelzebub, warns about an unclean spirit’s return, and rebukes sign-seekers with Jonah, Nineveh, and the queen of the south. He teaches about light and the eye, pronounces woes on Pharisees and lawyers, and opponents seek to accuse him.

documents.text: Therefore ye must always pray unto the Father in my name;
documents.context: The following passage is from **3 Nephi 18:19** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 39 verses and records Jesus instituting the sacrament with bread and wine among the disciples and multitude, commanding it be done in remembrance of his body and blood, and promising his Spirit to those who always remember him. He commands watchfulness and continual prayer, family prayer, meeting often, and welcoming seekers. He instructs disciples to forbid unworthy partaking without casting people out, to minister and pray for them, warns against disputations, gives disciples power to give the Holy Ghost, and ascends into heaven.

documents.text: But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Matthew 6:6** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 34 verses and records Jesus teaching to give alms, pray, and fast in secret rather than for public display, including the Lord’s Prayer and commands to forgive others. It contrasts earthly and heavenly treasures, discusses the single eye and serving God rather than mammon, and instructs not to be anxious about food, drink, or clothing, but to seek God’s kingdom first.

documents.text: Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watching thereunto with all perseverance and supplication for all saints;
documents.context: The following passage is from **Ephesians 6:18** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 24 verses and covers instructions for children to obey parents and for fathers to nurture without provoking; servants to obey masters sincerely and masters to forbear threatening. It urges believers to be strong, put on the whole armor of God against spiritual powers, and pray continually. Paul requests prayer for bold gospel speech as an imprisoned ambassador, sends Tychicus with news, and closes with peace and grace.

documents.text: And when thou prayest thou shalt not do as the hypocrites, for they love to pray, standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, they have their reward.
documents.context: The following passage is from **3 Nephi 13:5** from the **Book of Mormon**. Jesus charges the twelve to minister and teaches not to worry about food, drink, or clothing, but to seek God’s kingdom first.

documents.text: Be not ye therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.

It commands rejoicing, continual prayer, thanksgiving, not quenching the Spirit, valuing prophecy, testing all things, and avoiding evil, and closes with a sanctification prayer, greetings, and a charge to read the letter.

documents.text: And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us:

It states confidence in prayer according to God’s will, guidance about praying for a sin not unto death, assurance against the wicked one, and a warning to avoid idols.

documents.text: And it came to pass that when Jesus had thus prayed unto the Father, he came unto his disciples, and behold, they did still continue, without ceasing, to pray unto him; and they did not multiply many words, for it was given unto them what they should pray, and they were filled with desire.
documents.context: The following passage is from **3 Nephi 19:24** from the **Book of Mormon**. query: What does scripture say about repentance?

documents.text: Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord;
documents.context: The following passage is from **Acts 3:19** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 26 verses and records Peter and John healing a man lame from birth at the temple gate called Beautiful, causing public amazement in Solomon’s porch. Peter attributes the miracle to faith in Jesus Christ, recounts Israel’s rejection of Jesus before Pilate, and testifies of Jesus’ resurrection. He calls for repentance, cites Moses and the prophets, references the Abrahamic covenant, and states that Jesus is sent first to bless Israel by turning people from iniquities.

documents.text: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Luke 13:3** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 35 verses and records Jesus teaching that disasters do not prove greater guilt and calling all to repent; he gives the parable of the barren fig tree. In a synagogue on the sabbath he heals a woman bowed eighteen years and answers the ruler. He compares God’s kingdom to mustard seed and leaven, teaches about the narrow gate and exclusion, notes people from all directions entering. Pharisees warn of Herod; Jesus speaks of his mission and laments Jerusalem’s rejection.

documents.text: But if ye will repent and return unto the Lord your God I will turn away mine anger, saith the Lord; yea, thus saith the Lord, blessed are they who will repent and turn unto me, but wo unto him that repenteth not.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Helaman 13:11** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 39 verses and records Samuel the Lamanite preaching repentance at Zarahemla from the city wall after being cast out. He prophesies destruction within 400 years unless the Nephites repent and have faith in Jesus Christ. He warns Zarahemla, Gideon, and surrounding cities, foretells curses on the land and “slippery” hidden treasures, condemns persecuting prophets and trusting flattering teachers, and declares probation ending through procrastination.

documents.text: For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.
documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Corinthians 7:10** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 16 verses and records Paul urging believers to cleanse themselves and pursue holiness, defending his conduct toward the Corinthians. He describes troubles in Macedonia and comfort received through Titus’s arrival and report of their desire, mourning, and zeal. Paul explains his earlier letter caused temporary sorrow leading to repentance, contrasts godly and worldly sorrow, notes their renewed obedience, and expresses joy, comfort, and confidence in them.

documents.text: And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Matthew 3:2** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 17 verses and records John the Baptist preaching repentance in the wilderness of Judea, baptizing in the Jordan as people confess sins, and warning Pharisees and Sadducees to produce worthy fruit. John describes one coming after him who baptizes with the Holy Ghost and fire and brings judgment. Jesus comes from Galilee, is baptized by John, the Spirit descends like a dove, and a heavenly voice identifies Jesus as God’s beloved Son.

It foretells the Spirit poured on all flesh, cosmic signs, and deliverance for those calling on the LORD in Zion and Jerusalem.

documents.text: Therefore also now, saith the LORD, turn ye even to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning:

documents.text: Repent therefore of this thy wickedness, and pray God, if perhaps the thought of thine heart may be forgiven thee.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Acts 8:22** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 40 verses and records persecution after Stephen’s death, with believers scattered from Jerusalem while Saul imprisons many. Philip preaches in Samaria, performs healings and exorcisms, and many are baptized, including Simon the sorcerer. Peter and John confer the Holy Ghost by laying on hands; Simon is rebuked for offering money. Philip later baptizes an Ethiopian eunuch on the Gaza road and then preaches from Azotus to Caesarea.

documents.text: And they went out, and preached that men should repent.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mark 6:12** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 56 verses and records Jesus teaching in his hometown synagogue and being rejected, healing a few, and traveling to teach. Herod hears of Jesus and the chapter recounts John the Baptist’s imprisonment and beheading. Jesus feeds five thousand, walks on the sea, reaches Gennesaret, and heals many who touch him.

documents.text: And wo unto him to whom he shall say this, for it shall be unto him that will do iniquity, and he cannot be saved; therefore, for this cause, that men might be saved, hath repentance been declared.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Helaman 12:22** from the **Book of Mormon**. It states God’s power to command earth, mountains, waters, and the length of day, and to curse hidden treasures and individuals for iniquity. It declares repentance as the means of salvation and contrasts final outcomes of everlasting life versus damnation.

documents.text: And him that repenteth not of his sins, and confesseth them not, ye shall bring before the church, and do with him as the scripture saith unto you, either by commandment or by revelation.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 64:12** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. It names Joseph Smith and affirms keys with conditions of obedience, addresses sins of Ezra Booth, Isaac Morley, and Edward Partridge, and gives instructions about farms, business, and moving to Zion. It teaches sacrifice and tithing, warns of burning upon the wicked, outlines stewardship and judging in Zion, and foretells Zion’s flourishing and gathering.

documents.text: Know ye that ye must come unto repentance, or ye cannot be saved.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mormon 7:3** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 10 verses and records Mormon addressing the spared remnant of the house of Israel. He states they are Israel and must repent to be saved, lay down weapons, and stop shedding blood unless God commands. He urges belief in Jesus Christ’s death and resurrection, teaching resurrection and judgment. He commands repentance and baptism, referencing additional records, and identifies them as Jacob’s remnant of the first covenant.

documents.text: And now, my brethren, I would that, after ye have received so many witnesses, seeing that the holy scriptures testify of these things, ye come forth and bring fruit unto repentance.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 34:30** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 41 verses and records Amulek teaching the Zoramites about Christ’s coming and the need for an infinite, eternal atonement that fulfills the law of Moses. He explains mercy and justice, urges faith unto repentance, continual prayer in all places, and charity to the needy. He warns against procrastinating repentance, describes the state after death, and exhorts humility, taking Christ’s name, resisting the devil, patience in afflictions, and hope of rest.

documents.text: And that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Luke 24:47** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 53 verses and records women finding Jesus’ empty tomb, two angels announcing his resurrection, and the report to the apostles; Peter visits the sepulchre. Jesus appears to two disciples on the road to Emmaus, explains scriptures, is recognized in breaking bread, and vanishes. He appears to the gathered disciples, shows his hands and feet, eats food, commissions preaching repentance and remission of sins, promises power from on high, and ascends near Bethany.

documents.text: And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Jonah 3:10** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 10 verses and records the LORD commanding Jonah a second time to preach in Nineveh. Jonah goes to the great city and proclaims that in forty days Nineveh will be overthrown. The people believe God, fast, and wear sackcloth. The king decrees fasting for people and animals and calls for turning from evil and violence. God sees their repentance and does not bring the announced destruction.

query: What is the role of the Holy Ghost?

This chapter contains 31 verses and records Jesus consoling his disciples, promising to prepare a place in the Father’s house and to return. He commands keeping his commandments, promises the Comforter/Holy Ghost, gives peace, foretells his departure, and mentions the prince of this world.

They are transfigured, forbidden to reveal what they see, and continue ministering, baptizing, and giving the Holy Ghost. They escape prisons, pits, furnaces, and beasts unharmed; Mormon notes their future ministry among Gentiles, Jews, and Israel and explains their bodily change until judgment.

It describes earth’s sanctification and cosmic order, gives a parable of laborers, and commands prayer, sanctification, study, and organizing a school and house of God. It outlines end-time judgments, angels and trumpets, the Millennium, Michael’s battle, and rules for the School of the Prophets, including salutations and washing of feet.

Jesus Christ identifies Himself and states He will bring the fulness of the gospel from the Gentiles to Israel, calling David to assist.

He gives guidance on eating meat sold or served, abstaining if identified as idol-sacrifice, and commands doing all to God’s glory without offending Jews, Gentiles, or the church.

documents.text: And we are willing to enter into a covenant with our God to do his will, and to be obedient to his commandments in all things that he shall command us, all the remainder of our days, that we may not bring upon ourselves a never-ending torment, as has been spoken by the angel, that we may not drink out of the cup of the wrath of God.

query: What does scripture say about obedience?

documents.text: And thou shalt return and obey the voice of the LORD, and do all his commandments which I command thee this day.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Deuteronomy 30:8** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 20 verses and records Moses promising Israel’s restoration if they repent and obey: God gathers them from exile, returns them to their land, prospers them, and “circumcises” their heart; curses fall on enemies. It states the commandment is accessible and near. Moses sets before them life and death, blessing and curse, urges choosing life by loving and obeying the LORD, warning against idolatry and perishing.

documents.text: If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land:
documents.context: The following passage is from **Isaiah 1:19** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Isaiah’s vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah. It indicts Israel’s rebellion, moral corruption, and desolation, and rejects hypocritical sacrifices and assemblies. It commands repentance, justice for the oppressed, and care for the fatherless and widow. It contrasts promised cleansing and restoration of Zion with judgment on rebels and idolaters.

documents.text: Whether it be good, or whether it be evil, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we send thee; that it may be well with us, when we obey the voice of the LORD our God.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Jeremiah 42:6** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 22 verses and records Judah’s remnant, led by Johanan, asking Jeremiah to pray for guidance and pledging obedience. After ten days Jeremiah delivers the LORD’s word: remain in the land and God will build and plant them, show mercy, and protect them from the king of Babylon. If they go to Egypt, sword, famine, and pestilence will overtake them; they are warned not to go and are accused of dissembling.

documents.text: A blessing, if ye obey the commandments of the LORD your God, which I command you this day:
documents.context: The following passage is from **Deuteronomy 11:27** from the **Old Testament**. It contrasts Canaan with Egypt, promises rain and produce for obedience, warns against idolatry and drought, commands teaching and inscribing the words, defines borders, and sets blessing and curse on Gerizim and Ebal.

documents.text: Thou shalt therefore obey the voice of the LORD thy God, and do his commandments and his statutes, which I command thee this day.

They instruct setting up plastered stones on Mount Ebal, writing the law on them, building an uncut-stone altar, and offering burnt and peace offerings. Tribes stand on Gerizim and Ebal for blessings and curses, and Levites pronounce curses for idolatry, dishonoring parents, injustice, sexual sins, violence, bribery, and failing to keep the law.

documents.text: And Samuel said, Hath the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.

query: What is the plan of salvation?

documents.text: And now, behold, I say unto you: This is the plan of salvation unto all men, through the blood of mine Only Begotten, who shall come in the meridian of time.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Moses 6:62** from the **Pearl of Great Price**. This chapter contains 68 verses and records Adam calling his sons to repent; Seth’s birth and worship; a book of remembrance and priesthood; genealogies from Adam to Enoch; increasing wickedness, wars, and secret works; Enoch’s prophetic call, visions, and preaching in the land of Cainan; and God’s instructions to Adam on repentance, baptism in Jesus Christ’s name, the Holy Ghost, and Adam’s baptism and spiritual rebirth.

documents.text: We believe that through the Atonement of Christ, all mankind may be saved, by obedience to the laws and ordinances of the Gospel.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Articles of Faith 1:3** from the **Pearl of Great Price**. This chapter contains 13 verses and records thirteen Articles of Faith: belief in the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost; accountability for personal sin; salvation through Christ’s Atonement by gospel obedience; faith, repentance, baptism, and laying on of hands; divine calling and authority; church offices; spiritual gifts; scripture (Bible and Book of Mormon); continuing revelation; gathering of Israel, Zion, and Christ’s reign; religious freedom; civic obedience; and moral virtues and doing good.

documents.text: Now, if it had not been for the plan of redemption, which was laid from the foundation of the world, there could have been no resurrection of the dead; but there was a plan of redemption laid, which shall bring to pass the resurrection of the dead, of which has been spoken.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 12:25** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 37 verses and records Alma addressing Zeezrom and the people, exposing his deceit and warning of the devil’s snares. Alma explains that mysteries are given according to heed and a softened heart; hardened hearts receive less and are led to destruction. He teaches resurrection and judgment by works, including a second spiritual death for the unrepentant. Answering Antionah, Alma recounts Adam’s fall, the tree of life restriction, probationary life, angels, commandments, redemption, repentance, and entering God’s rest.

documents.text: That through his atonement, and by obedience to the principles of the gospel, mankind might be saved.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 138:4** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 60 verses and records Joseph F. Smith’s 1918 vision of the spirit world while pondering 1 Peter. He sees righteous spirits assembled awaiting Christ, who preaches resurrection and redemption to them. Christ does not visit the wicked but commissions righteous messengers to preach repentance, faith, and vicarious ordinances to spirits in darkness. Adam, Eve, Abel, Noah, Abraham, Moses, prophets, Nephite prophets, and latter-day leaders are present; temple work and continued missionary labor among the dead are described.

documents.text: And now remember, my son, if it were not for the plan of redemption, (laying it aside) as soon as they were dead their souls were miserable, being cut off from the presence of the Lord.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 42:11** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Alma explaining to his son the justice of God in punishing sin. He recounts Adam and Eve being cast from Eden, barred from the tree of life, and given a probationary time to repent. He outlines temporal and spiritual death, law and punishment, and repentance. He states mercy operates through an atonement, bringing resurrection, restoration to God’s presence, and judgment by works, urging repentance and preaching.

documents.text: O how great the plan of our God! For on the other hand, the paradise of God must deliver up the spirits of the righteous, and the grave deliver up the body of the righteous; and the spirit and the body is restored to itself again, and all men become incorruptible, and immortal, and they are living souls, having a perfect knowledge like unto us in the flesh, save it be that our knowledge shall be perfect.
documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Nephi 9:13** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 54 verses and records Jacob teaching about the Lord’s covenants with Israel, the fall, death, resurrection, and an infinite atonement. He describes judgment, paradise, hell, and restoration of body and spirit. He commands repentance, faith, baptism, and enduring to the end, explains accountability under law, pronounces woes on specific sins, and urges humility, prayer, and coming to the Holy One of Israel.

documents.text: And now I say unto you that the time shall come that the salvation of the Lord shall be declared to every nation, kindred, tongue, and people.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mosiah 15:28** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Abinadi teaching that God comes among men as Father and Son, suffers, is crucified, and overcomes death to intercede and redeem. He defines Christ’s “seed” as prophets and believers who heed their words. He quotes Isaiah on publishing peace and salvation.
